extracted.intended_audience: IP scholars, patent policymakers, patent office officials, and practitioners interested in patent examination quality
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the quality of patent examination and issued patents using markers of substantive examiner engagement, claim-disclosure fidelity, and system-level reforms to focus resources on high-stakes patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triage Toward High-Stakes Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective examination should concentrate scrutiny on patents most likely to be commercially valuable (e.g., pharmaceutical compositions, claims drafted with broad commercial reach). Ex post mechanisms (post-grant review, IPR) should bear the validity-determination burden for the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize examination resources on patents where validity will have large social/commercial consequences; accept that exhaustive ex ante examination for every patent is socially wasteful. Use applicant election (fee/track) or triage criteria to allocate 'gold-plated' examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure-Based Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Even patents that will never be litigated must serve the disclosure function: examiner quality work includes ensuring claims are clearly tied to specification disclosure even when validity will not be tested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that claim scope corresponds to the specification; look for written-description and enablement support. Examiner should reject or require amendment where claims reach beyond described embodiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be clear enough that a competitor reading the patent can determine its scope without litigation. Failure of notice (vague boundaries, functional language untethered to structure) is a quality defect even if the patent is never enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate claim clarity and boundaries; avoid untethered functional claiming. Prefer claim language that a POSITA can interpret without resort to costly litigation; use 112 doctrine to police indefiniteness and functional breadth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine grants without substantive prior-art rejections (marker of low-quality examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants issued routinely without examiner-authored or substantive prior-art rejections indicate low-quality examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag first-action allowances or allowances after only applicant-cited art. High rates of such routine grants suggest insufficient independent searching and cursory examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-action allowances of broad genus claims without examiner-cited art (marker of low-quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing broad genus claims at first action without the examiner citing relevant prior art is a sign of poor examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad genus/claiming should trigger independent search and substantive rejections if art exists; absence of examiner-cited art for broad claims is an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner reliance solely on applicant-cited art (marker of low-quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: When examiners rely exclusively on prior art submitted by applicants (IDS) and do not conduct independent searches, examination quality is suspect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality examination entails examiner-initiated searches and citation of art beyond the applicant's disclosures. Routine acceptance of applicant-cited art only is inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance of claims using functional language without 112(f) treatment or written description support (marker of low-quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitting functional claim language that lacks proper 112(f) structure or written-description support indicates poor scrutiny of claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply 35 U.S.C. §112 standards: require corresponding structure, material, or acts for functional claiming, or treat such claims under 112(f)/means-plus-function rules. Reject or require narrowing where written description is missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: High allowance rates correlated with experienced-examiner short-cutting (marker of low-quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that experienced examiners with high allowance rates may be short-cutting examination processes is a marker of poor examination quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use allowance-rate metrics cautiously but watch for statistical correlations between allowance rates and lack of substantive prosecution; investigate patterns of shortcutting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple substantive office actions identifying prior art outside applicant's IDS (marker of high-quality examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner-initiated, substantive office actions that cite prior art not submitted by the applicant indicate thorough independent searching and engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple rounds of substantive rejections and citations to independent art show meaningful examination. Prefer examiners who supplement applicant-cited references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner-initiated claim amendments that narrow overbroad terms (marker of high-quality examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: When examiners propose or require claim amendments that narrow overbroad claim language, it demonstrates active policing of claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for examiner-driven narrowing amendments during prosecution; this is evidence of quality work to align claims with patentability and disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of foreign-language or non-patent literature prior art (marker of high-quality examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of non-patent literature and foreign-language sources by examiners reflects deeper prior-art searching and higher examination quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing diverse information sources (NPL, foreign patents/papers) improves art coverage. Citation of such sources is a positive signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive 112 rejections rather than purely 102/103 (marker of high-quality examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuing substantive written-description, enablement, or indefiniteness rejections shows attention to disclosure and claim clarity beyond obviousness/novelty questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize 112 issues where claims appear untethered to the specification; substantive 112 activity indicates careful review of the disclosure function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final claim language that maps clearly onto specification disclosure (marker of high-quality examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: High-quality examination yields issued claims whose language corresponds clearly to the patent specification and disclosed embodiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess issued claims for a clear mapping to specification terms and embodiments; absence of mapping indicates weaker quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement (critical quality dimension for issued patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: A POSITA could practice the full claim scope from the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the specification teaches how to make and use the full claimed invention across its full scope. Lack of enablement supports invalidity or narrowing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Description (critical quality dimension for issued patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant possessed the full claim scope at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for demonstrable possession of claimed subject matter in the application as filed; claims that extend beyond the original disclosure should be scrutinized or rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice (critical quality dimension for issued patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim boundaries are knowable without expensive claim-construction litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess claims for definiteness and clarity from the perspective of competitors and POSITA. Ambiguous claim scope undermines the notice function of patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-Matter Eligibility (critical quality dimension for issued patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim does not preempt an abstract idea or natural phenomenon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply eligibility doctrines to ensure that claims are limited to patent-eligible subject matter and do not improperly preempt fundamental building blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Obviousness (critical quality dimension for issued patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: A POSITA reviewing the cited art would not have arrived at the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the claimed invention represents more than the predictable use or combination of prior art; substantive 103 analysis should be evident in prosecution where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent search beyond applicant-cited art (operative test question)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the examiner conduct an independent search beyond applicant-cited art?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of examiner-found art (not just IDS) is a positive sign; absence suggests cursory examination. Look for citations to art found by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressed substantive 112 issues (operative test question)
rubrics_metrics.description: Were the substantive 112 issues (enablement, written description, indefiniteness) addressed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review prosecution history for substantive 112 rejections or discussions; absence may indicate failure to police disclosure quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims clearly tied to specification disclosure (operative test question)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the final claims clearly tied to specification disclosure?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine claim language vs. specification to confirm a clear mapping; lack of mapping suggests weak examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent third party can know scope (operative test question)
rubrics_metrics.description: Would a competent third party reading the patent know what is and isn't covered?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the notice function from a POSITA/competitor perspective. If the scope is unclear without litigation, quality is deficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution history shows genuine engagement (operative test question)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the prosecution history show genuine engagement with patentability, not formulaic exchanges?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for substantive back-and-forth, meaningful rejections, and reasoned examiner explanations rather than boilerplate or formulaic allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiered Examination (reform proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional gold-plated examination for applicants who want stronger validity presumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer applicants the choice to pay for more thorough ex ante examination (better searching, more substantive review) in exchange for stronger presumptions of validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust Post-Grant Review (reform proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cheap administrative challenges to weed out invalid patents that become commercially significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengthen post-grant administrative mechanisms (e.g., IPR/post-grant review) so that resources focus on adjudicating validity where it matters most.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced Validity Presumption (reform proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issued patents should not enjoy strong presumptions of validity given the limits of ex ante examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust doctrines and standards so that an issued patent's validity is not overly insulated from challenge because ex parte examination is constrained by rational ignorance.
